subject.title: fix(ui): add timeout to chat avatar metadata fetch

question: Should chat-avatar metadata requests fail after a fixed five-second delay, or should this path use another shared request-lifetime policy?
rationale: Current code and documentation define no Control UI latency threshold, and selecting five seconds can intentionally replace eventual success with cleared state on slower deployments.

options.title: Keep five seconds with proof
options.body: Retain the proposed cutoff after a real delayed-request run shows that it improves recovery without rejecting a supported deployment.

options.title: Use a shared timeout policy
options.body: Replace the literal with an owner-approved shared Control UI request-lifetime value or lifecycle signal and test that policy.

options.title: Keep requests unbounded
options.body: Pause or close the PR if maintainers prefer stale-result guards without an elapsed-time failure threshold.

recommendation.title: Keep five seconds with proof
recommendation.body: Retain the proposed cutoff after a real delayed-request run shows that it improves recovery without rejecting a supported deployment.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current avatar request module and are the strongest history-backed owner for its request-lifetime policy.
